title: Elders
definition: Elders are qualified spiritual leaders called to shepherd, oversee, teach, and care for the local church under Christ.
summary: Elders are qualified men called to shepherd, oversee, teach, and guard the local church under Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the Chief Shepherd, and elders serve under His authority for the good of the flock.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Elders are qualified shepherds called to oversee, teach, protect, and care for the church. Scripture ties this role to character, doctrine, humility, and spiritual watchfulness.

Eldership is not a title for control or status. It is accountable shepherding under Christ, requiring sober responsibility for souls and faithfulness to the Word.

Jesus is the Chief Shepherd. Every faithful elder serves under His authority and must reflect His care, truth, patience, and courage.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because churches can be harmed by unqualified leadership or by suspicion toward all leadership. Biblical eldership gives the church a standard for shepherds who lead through truth and character, not manipulation.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Pray for elders, test leadership by Scripture, and honor faithful shepherding without idolizing leaders. If entrusted with leadership, pursue holiness, sound doctrine, and gentle courage before God.
